body:
Pass 44. Correcting my own advice and sharpening the finding.

I told you the Rd examples could be lifted from the README. I then executed all 11 README blocks: 7 run clean, 3 fail - lm_extractor (object X not found), lm_relation_fit (response_runs not found), plan_crossnobis (fit not found). They are illustrative placeholders, which is fine as a style, but it means those three cannot be lifted. My advice holds for the 7 that start from precomputed effect matrices only.

Sharper finding from checking the vignettes: introduction.Rmd has lm_extractor in exactly one chunk and it is eval=FALSE (line 347); lm_relation_fit appears only in prose; and crossnobis appears ZERO times in either vignette. So the raw-fMRI entry path has no executable documentation anywhere - placeholder in README, eval=FALSE in vignette, no Rd example - and nothing outside the test suite runs it. The crossnobis capability that Epics 5-7 built has Rd examples but no vignette presence at all.

That is what makes your criterion bite: the first user journey starts at response data, not at a precomputed effect matrix, and that entry is the least documented part of the package.

One small self-contained raw-data fixture solves all three: Rd example for lm_relation_fit/lm_extractor, replacement for the eval=FALSE chunk, and the first-journey example. Write once, reference three times.
